# Retrieval benchmark: BM25 vs local embeddings

<!-- Generated by scripts/benchmark_retrieval.py. Do not edit by hand; re-run the script instead. -->

24 queries over 20 chunks, k=3. Query mix: 12 lexical, 12 paraphrase.

```bash
pip install -r requirements-bench.txt
python scripts/benchmark_retrieval.py
```

| Backend | all recall@3 / MRR | lexical recall@3 / MRR | paraphrase recall@3 / MRR |
|---|---|---|---|
| BM25 (deployed) | 0.75 / 0.74 | 1.00 / 1.00 | 0.50 / 0.47 |
| MiniLM embeddings | 0.94 / 0.93 | 1.00 / 1.00 | 0.88 / 0.85 |

**lexical** queries share vocabulary with the target chunk; **paraphrase**
queries deliberately do not. The split matters because lexical overlap is
precisely what BM25 is built to exploit, so a single aggregate number would
flatter it.

Embeddings run locally via sentence-transformers, so these numbers are
reproducible without an API key. The deployed service still uses BM25: see
the interpretation in DECISIONS.md.
